subject: Putting the result of combine.subsets into a geomorph.data.frame

messages.author: 600ad4bb25ddcc99
messages.subject: Putting the result of combine.subsets into a geomorph.data.frame
parts:
Hello,

I would like to put the result of combine.subsets into a gdf together with some further ecological and taxonomic data. The separate landmarks sets are objects of class gpagen.
My code looks like this:

gpa.all <- combine.subsets(set1= gpa.set1, set2= gpa.set2, gpa = T)
gdf.all <- geomorph.data.frame(gpa.all, species = paste(set1$genusspecies), sex =  set1$sex, family =  set1$family, genus =  set1$genus, wlen.set1 =  set1$fw.l, etc., etc.)

I get the following error message:
Error in geomorph.data.frame(gpa.all) :
  Some input is either dimensionless or inappropriate for data frames

Looking at the structure of the combine.subsets object, it appears that maybe geomorph.data.frame does not want to eat lists with two sublayers (or more)? (haven't tried it with other lists within lists)

My workaround right now is to put the (sub)lists I need from gpa.all into the gdf one by one, but I was wondering whether there is a more elegant way to do this or maybe I missed something regarding this specific workflow?

Thanks for any input on this!

Alex
